column6: What was discussed
column7: Real World Scenario

column3: Publicly accessible S3 buckets, Azure Blob containers, GCP storage buckets with PII/PCI/PHI.
column6: Supported out-of-the-box. Can scan cloud storage and highlight publicly accessed buckets.
column7: A marketing team accidentally sets an Azure Blob container holding a CSV of 10,000 customer credit card applications to 'Public read access'.

column3: Sensitive data stores without encryption (CMK or CSP-managed acceptable depending on policy).
column6: Supported out-of-the-box. Identifies unencrypted data. If a file is encrypted, it skips scanning the content but correctly flags it as encrypted.
column7: A database snapshot containing employee SINs is saved to a storage bucket without KMS or Azure Key Vault encryption enabled.

column3: TLS not enforced for databases, storage endpoints, APIs handling sensitive data.
column6: Supported. Though technically in transit, it is supported by the tool.
column7: An internal legacy application sends daily transaction logs with unmasked account numbers over HTTP instead of HTTPS to a cloud analytics tool.

column3: *:* or admin-level access to data stores with sensitive data.
column6: Supported where permission metadata is available (e.g., requires AD integration for on-prem). Users can run reports to see who has access, and custom risk policies are in development.
column7: The 'Domain Users' Active Directory group is mistakenly given read access to a SharePoint folder containing executive bonus structures and unredacted financial reports.

column3: Sensitive datasets shared with untrusted or external accounts/projects/subscriptions.
column6: Supported. Can define external sharing rules and alert on untrusted/external emails with access.
column7: A developer shares an Azure subscription containing live customer transaction data with an external contractor's personal Gmail account instead of their corporate identity.

column2: Sensitive data in unapproved regions (data residency violations)
column3: PCI/PII data stored outside Canada/US/EU (depending on jurisdiction).
column6: Supported. Data residency violations are detected based on comprehensive findings (e.g., specific regional IDs/addresses) rather than simple keywords. Custom data classes can also be created.
column7: GDPR-protected data containing UK citizen passport numbers is detected in a US-East Azure region due to an improper automated backup script.

column2: Snapshots/backups of sensitive data without encryption or with public access
column3: EBS, Azure Managed Disks, GCP Persistent Disk snapshots.
column6: Partially supported. Noted as a 'nice-to-have' since other systems handle similar functions; team will review and adjust requirements.
column7: A database administrator creates a quick, unencrypted snapshot of an Azure SQL database holding customer loan profiles for testing purposes.

column2: Sensitive data accessible by compute with public exposure
column3: VM, container, or function with internet access and permissions to sensitive data.
column6: Supported straight away.
column7: An Azure Virtual Machine running an internal data visualization dashboard with live customer PII is accidentally given a public IP address.

column3: Sensitive data duplicated in non-approved or shadow data stores.
column6: Supported. Can identify duplicates based on matching file size, data class, and creation date (metadata), though it doesn't do deep hash checking. Further duplicate detection is on the product roadmap.
column7: A data scientist downloads a subset of production transaction data to their personal OneDrive for a quick Power BI analysis and forgets to delete it.

column3: Sensitive data in buckets/databases not accessed in >90 days but still exposed.
column6: Supported. Identifies dormant data (e.g., older than 90 days) that is still exposed.
column7: A decommissioned HR application's backend database, untouched for 3 years, still exists in the cloud containing former employee direct deposit details.

column2: Lack of logging/monitoring for sensitive data access
column3: No CloudTrail/Activity Logs/Azure Monitor/Cloud Audit Logs enabled for access.
column6: Supported. Correlates sensitive data stores with available cloud monitoring signals and flags if logging/monitoring is missing.
column7: A storage bucket holding archived wire transfer records has CloudTrail or Azure object-level logging disabled, meaning no one knows who accessed it last week.

column2: IAM misconfigurations giving broad group/user access
column3: AD groups, GCP IAM bindings, AWS IAM groups with excessive data access.
column6: Supported. Inspects ACLs to see who has access, allowing for detailed access reporting.
column7: A service account designed for an automated reporting pipeline is given 'Owner' permissions across the entire cloud tenant rather than just read access to the specific data lake.

column3: Sensitive data stores accessible from untrusted networks/IPs.
column6: Partially supported. DSPM is primarily focused on data at rest; data in motion use cases are better covered by Proofpoint's DLP platform.
column7: Customer data is accessed by an administrative account from an IP address block bypassing VPN routing requirements established by the Azure Virtual Network Manager (AVNM).

column3: No labeling/tagging for PII/PCI across datasets.
column6: Supported. Can automatically reclassify data if it lacks a classification tag.
column7: A newly created folder in SharePoint meant to hold pre-release earnings reports has no sensitivity labels applied, allowing it to bypass DLP rules.

column3: Relying solely on CSP-managed default keys instead of CMK where policy requires CMK.
column6: Supported. Can identify if default/CSP keys (like Amazon's keys) are used instead of customer-managed keys, and flags it as a risk.
column7: A storage account holding sensitive internal M&A documents is encrypted using default CSP keys rather than the enterprise's mandated Customer-Managed Keys (CMK).

column2: Inactive identities with access to sensitive data
column3: User/service accounts dormant >90 days but retaining access.
column6: Supported. Correlates with ACLs to flag users who haven't logged in within 90 days but still have access to sensitive data.
column7: A former vendor's account, which hasn't logged in for 6 months, still retains active read permissions to the cloud financial forecasting model.

column2: Inconsistent backup and retention for sensitive datasets
column3: Missing or misaligned retention policies for PCI/PII data.
column6: Partially supported. Can identify datasets that should be governed, but actual backup validation depends on the underlying backup tool.
column7: A repository of historical trading data is only retained for 1 year, violating regulations that mandate a 7-year retention policy for that specific data class.

column2: Sensitive data accessible by over-privileged service accounts
column3: Functions, pipelines, or automation accounts with broad data access.
column6: Supported. Highlights sensitive assets exposed to service accounts or excessively large groups.
column7: A GitHub Actions runner is assigned an over-privileged service principal that can read all Blob storage containers, not just the one required for its deployment job.

column3: Multiple redundant storage of sensitive data in different accounts/projects.
column6: Low priority. Handled similarly to shadow copies/duplicates (#9).
column7: Three identical copies of a high-value customer contact list exist across SharePoint, a Google Workspace drive, and an old Azure File Share.

column3: Databases/storage accounts without owner or business context tags.
column6: Not supported out-of-the-box, but users can implement it by building a custom risk policy.
column7: The security team discovers an orphaned RDS instance that was spun up by a former employee two years ago and contains an unknown cache of user emails.

column3: Sensitive datasets retained beyond business/regulatory need.
column6: Currently not available, but slated as a Q3 feature on the roadmap.
column7: Customer data from a marketing campaign from 2018 is still being kept in an active database, violating the company's 3-year data destruction policy.

column3: Non-aligned encryption algorithms across multi-cloud (e.g., AES-128 instead of AES-256).
column6: Not primarily a DSPM function; this relates more to crypto standards enforced by compliance.
column7: A legacy script encrypts files using outdated AES-128 before uploading them to the cloud, failing to meet the modern AES-256 standard required by enterprise architecture.

column3: Multiple IAM bindings/policies leading to complexity and potential drift.
column6: Low priority. Discussed briefly regarding multiple bindings and IGA vs DBMS, marked as low priority.
column7: A user has restricted access to a folder via Azure AD group policies, but an overarching IAM role gives them full read access to the entire underlying storage bucket, creating a permission conflict.
